title: Maré: live truth on a ready-made storefront
summary: The ready-made pages stay; only price, stock and the bag are live, in one small shared request; stock is shown honestly; adding to the bag is instant only when it's safe; busy mode is designed; checkout stays light; speed is measured in sales.

steps.title: Keep what works
steps.caption: The store's pages are built ahead of time and served from nearby, which is why they're fast and cheap. That stays exactly as it is.
steps.engineering: Static-first Astro with small islands, a 60 kB JS budget and CLS 0; HTML cached for days and purged by surrogate key; the Black Friday price book is baked in.
steps.presenterNote: The current storefront is fast because it's ready-made. The job is to keep that and fix only what it can't do.

steps.title: Only a small part is live
steps.caption: Price, stock and the bag come in one small request per page. Ten thousand shoppers on one deal ask our systems once every 2 seconds.
steps.engineering: One batched /live call for the visible SKUs; about 2 s of edge micro-cache with request coalescing; the price book version in the HTML is confirmed by the live slot.
steps.presenterNote: Only the parts that change every second are live, and one shared answer serves everyone looking at the same deal.

steps.title: Honest stock
steps.caption: Stock shows as in stock, few left or sold out. It's always true, and the exact count is checked the moment you add to bag.
steps.engineering: Bands cache well and rarely change; the reservation is the only exact read. A precise '3 left' that is wrong half the time costs more trust than it earns.
steps.presenterNote: A precise number that's often wrong is worse than a simple one that's always right.

steps.title: Add to bag, safely
steps.caption: When there's plenty, the bag updates instantly. When only a few are left, it says reserving and confirms, so we never promise what's gone.
steps.engineering: Optimistic UI for In stock, confirmed for Few left; a client-generated idempotency key per click; a bag mirror in localStorage reconciled with the server.
steps.presenterNote: Instant feels great until it's wrong, so the page is instant only when it's safe to be.

steps.title: Busy mode is designed
steps.caption: When our systems are under pressure, the page swaps extras for simpler versions it already has. Nothing breaks, and buying still works.
steps.engineering: Level L0–L4 arrives in a response header; each island declares a tier; fallbacks are rendered at build time, so degrading fetches nothing new.
steps.presenterNote: Every extra on the page has a calm, simpler twin ready, so a busy night looks simpler, not broken.

steps.title: The buy path stays light
steps.caption: Checkout loads nothing extra, not even marketing trackers, and starts loading while the bag is open, so paying feels instant.
steps.engineering: An isolated checkout bundle with no third-party tags (server-side events instead); checkout and payment fields are prefetched when the bag drawer opens.
steps.presenterNote: The path to paying is the one place where nothing is allowed to slow us down.

steps.title: Speed measured in reais
steps.caption: We measure speed on real phones and link it to sales, so we know which slow moment costs money and fix that one first.
steps.engineering: Field LCP, INP and CLS by page, busy level and device, joined to the funnel; traceparent on live, bag and checkout calls links each one to Tidewatch.
steps.presenterNote: Speed only matters when it costs sales, so we measure it in reais, not milliseconds.
